messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: paging: High KV cache amplification detected for region-us-west1; continuous-batching request rate spike +5x. Alerts: cache_evictions, kv_cache_growth, tail_latency_slo_breach. Root ts=1829123456

devon_oncall: seeing it too. customers affected? any 5xx spike?

sara_ops: 5xxs are flat but p95 token latency jumped from 45ms -> 520ms for several model endpoints. Top offender appears to be model-llama-2-7b / route: text.generate.

mike_sre: confirmed. KV cache pages going into OOM churn. Heap growth on infer-proxy-02 around 20:10 UTC.

jia_runtime: this smells like recent continuous-batching tweak (auto-prefix-merge) we rolled yesterday. Could be combining too many distinct prefixes into shared batches causing oversized KV lookups.

ana_support: flagging two paying customers who reported slow responses via support: acme-inc and bluefin-analytics. Both on dedicated pools in us-west1.

devon_oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) flip canary to reduce continuous batching aggressiveness 2) per-customer override for acme-inc + bluefin-analytics to disable continuous batching 3) deploy temporary kv_cache_ttl shorter on affected hosts. Anyone object?

sara_ops: +1 to per-customer disable. We should preserve isolation for large customers.

mike_sre: agree. Also enable extra logging for kv cache hits/misses for 30m before rolling back flags to get telemetry.

jia_runtime: I can run the flag changes. Proposed steps:
- set feature flag continuous_batching.merge_window_ms from 50 -> 10 for global canary (10% traffic)
- set per-customer override continuous_batching.enabled=false for acme-inc and bluefin-analytics
- apply kv_cache.tune: max_prefetch_keys=128 -> 64 and kv_cache.ttl_s=360 -> 120 on us-west1 pool

devon_oncall: rollout order: canary -> monitor 5m -> per-customer overrides -> monitor 10m -> widen if stable. Who will run canary?

jia_runtime: I'll run the canary now. Running command:```
# set 10% canary for the reduced merge window
redwood-ff apply continuous_batching.merge_window_ms=10 --canary 10 --description "emergency reduce merge window due to KV amplification"
```

ops-runner-bot: redwood-ff: change submitted (id=ff-20260314-01). Canaries scheduled.

mike_sre: monitoring dashboards: KV_cache_evictions, batch_size_histogram, p95_latency. Pulling logs for infer-proxy-02.

(2m passes)

jia_runtime: canary shows immediate drop in average batch size for canary traffic from ~85 -> ~16. KV cache lookups per request down ~60% on canary hosts.

devon_oncall: good. now applying per-customer overrides for acme-inc and bluefin-analytics. Command:
```
redwood-ff apply continuous_batching.enabled=false --scope customer:acme-inc,customer:bluefin-analytics --description "emergency per-customer disable for KV blowup mitigation"
```

ops-runner-bot: redwood-ff: per-customer overrides applied (id=ff-20260314-02).

ana_support: reaching out to Acme CS lead to let them know we've disabled continuous batching for them and are mitigating impact. Draft message: "We've temporarily disabled continuous batching on your endpoints to reduce latency. No code changes required. We'll keep you updated." Want to send now?

sara_ops: send now. Add note that performance may slightly change and we're monitoring.

ana_support: sent to Acme; they replied "Thanks, see improvement already."

mike_sre: us-west1 kv_cache_evictions down 72% in last 4 minutes. p95 latency trending to 110ms from peak 520ms. No 5xx increase. Looks promising.

devon_oncall: ok keep canary for 10 more minutes and if stable we can bump the global change or keep per-customer overrides until tomorrow when we can do deeper root cause. Also set paging to alert if cache_growth resumes beyond threshold.

jia_runtime: also applied temporary kv tuning settings on affected pool:```
kubectl -n inference patch configmap kv-cache-config -p ' {"data":{"max_prefetch_keys":"64","ttl_s":"120"}}' && kubectl rollout restart daemonset/infer-proxy-us-west1
```

ops-runner-bot: daemonset rollout started on infer-proxy-us-west1 (10 pods).

(6m passes)

mike_sre: infra note: some dedicated customer hosts still show elevated swap churn; I'm evicting a few heavy background jobs and increasing eviction pressure. Will keep you updated.

ana_support: Bluefin reports improved latency as well, but asks for ETA on permanent fix and whether we can avoid future breaks.

jia_runtime: short answer: we need to roll back the auto-prefix-merge heuristic or add prefix cardinality checks before merging. I'll schedule a PR to gate merges when distinct prefix keys > threshold. For now leave per-customer overrides in place for 24h.

devon_oncall: agree. Action items:
- jia_runtime: PR to add prefix cardinality threshold + revert aggressive merge heuristic (owner: jia, ETA: 24h)
- mike_sre: continue monitoring and remove background jobs from dedicated pools if needed (ETA: 1h)
- sara_ops: coordinate with support to notify affected customers and confirm performance (ongoing)
- devon_oncall: prepare post-incident notes and follow-up blameless RCA (owner: devon, draft due EOD)

mike_sre: adding a temporary dashboard panel to track per-customer KV cache growth and batch size distribution.

ops-runner-bot: alerting rule updated: kv_cache_growth[5m] > 2x baseline -> page eng-oncall.

devon_oncall: handing off to night on-call @mike_sre. If anyone sees regressions re-page. I'm going to sleep. Thanks all. :wave:

mike_sre: taking it. I'll keep the overrides until jia's PR lands and we have a tested patch. If stability persists tomorrow morning we can gradually re-enable for low-cardinality customers.

incident-bot: incident severity downgraded to SEV-2 at 1829123518; mitigation in place (per-customer overrides + canary + kv tuning). Please fill incident form: /incident fill "KV-cache amplification - continuous batching"

devon_oncall: posting quick TL;DR in #postmortems after form filled. Good job team. :thumbsup:

(End of thread)
